# Create a command (/docs/admin/connect-and-extend/commands)

A command fires only on the exact phrase. It never guesses.

## ✍️ Steps [#️-steps]

1. Open **Settings**, **Voice**, then the **Commands** card. Tap **Create a command**. Adults and above can do this.
2. Type a **Trigger phrase**, such as "movie night".
3. Under **Who can trigger this command**, pick the lowest role.
4. Under **What this command does**, pick one:
   - **Say something back**: type what MaiPai says, and optionally a spoken version.
   - **Control a smart-home device**: type the Home Assistant domain, the service and the entity id.
5. Tap **Create command**.

## 📋 Manage the list [#-manage-the-list]

Owners and admins open **Home settings**, then **Commands** to see **Household commands**. Each row shows its phrase, its action and the role needed. Tap **Delete** to remove one. You can delete your own commands. Owners and admins can delete any.

If it fails, Home says "Could not create that command." or "Could not delete that command."

## 🙋 Still need help? [#-still-need-help]

For smart-home setup, see [Notifications and Telegram](/docs/admin/connect-and-extend/notifications-and-telegram) or ask whoever set up Home Assistant.


# Notifications and Telegram (/docs/admin/connect-and-extend/notifications-and-telegram)

Home can tell people about things that matter: a backup failing, an update waiting, a new repair. Telegram and browser alerts stay off until a person turns them on.

## 🔔 Where alerts go [#-where-alerts-go]

| Channel | Who sets it up | Default |
|---|---|---|
| **Show alerts on this device** | Each person, under Settings, Notifications, Alerts | Off |
| Telegram | Owner or admin sets the bot, each person links a chat | Off |
| A robot | **Send time-sensitive notifications to a robot** | Off |

## 🤖 Set up Telegram [#-set-up-telegram]

Telegram uses one bot for the whole household. Messages go through Telegram's servers, so they leave your house. The [privacy page](/docs/admin/look-after-it/privacy-audit) lists the row.

1. In Telegram, message @BotFather and create a bot. Copy its token.
2. In Home, open **Settings**, **Home settings**, **Integrations**, then the **Telegram** card. Paste the token in **Telegram bot token**. It is stored encrypted.
3. Each person messages the bot once. The bot replies with a chat id.
4. Each person opens **Settings**, **Notifications**, **Telegram** and pastes it in **Your Telegram chat id**.
5. Each person ticks the **Telegram me when** switches they want.

All switches default to off. Examples, one per event:

- **Telegram me about new Repairs items**
- **Telegram me when backups start failing**
- **Telegram me when a MaiPai Home update is available**
- **Telegram me when a Stack engine reports an open warning or critical problem**
- **Telegram me when a model download fails**

Owners and admins will want the first three.

## 🌙 Quiet hours [#-quiet-hours]

Alerts wait during quiet hours, default 21:00 to 07:00. Set the household times with **Quiet hours start** and **Quiet hours end** on the **Telegram** card under Integrations. A person can set their own with **Personal quiet hours start** and **end**. A parent sets a child's. Safety alarms ignore quiet hours.

## 🔧 If nothing arrives [#-if-nothing-arrives]

1. Check the token has no spaces and the person messaged the bot first.
2. Check the chat id belongs to that person.
3. Check the event switch is on for that person.

No test-message button exists yet. Trigger a real alert to check, such as a model download.


# Add and remove packages (/docs/admin/connect-and-extend/packages)

A **package** adds one ability to Home, such as weather, a timer or a news shelf. Home itself ships as a set of packages, so nearly every feature is one.

## 📦 What comes with Home [#-what-comes-with-home]

Home includes 36 packages. They cover:

- **Daily help**: timer, reminders, lists, weather, currency, unit conversion, math, translation
- **Info**: news, sports, web search, media lookup, almanac (date, time, moon, holidays, on this day)
- **Learning and play**: tutor, trivia, jokes, bedtime storybook, music
- **Home control**: lights on and off, lock doors
- **Memory**: remember and recall
- **News feeds**: household feeds and kids' feeds

A shelf of apps on the Home screen is planned, not available yet.

## 🧒 Who can use a package [#-who-can-use-a-package]

Each package declares the lowest role that may use it. A child sees only what a child may use. Kids' news feeds, for example, are for children.

The child's **Limits** tab saves daily minutes for each kind of package. Enforcing them in the package host is planned, not available yet. See [Add people and parental controls](/docs/admin/people-and-safety/add-people-and-parental-controls).

## 🔒 What a package may do [#-what-a-package-may-do]

Every package lists the outside services it contacts, when and why. Those rows feed the [privacy audit](/docs/admin/look-after-it/privacy-audit). A package that contacts nothing adds no row.

## 🛒 Install, update and remove [#-install-update-and-remove]

Planned, not in the app yet: browsing the MaiPai catalog and installing packages from a screen. Home has no store page today.

The Home server already has the groundwork:

- A signed catalog index check, so a tampered catalog is rejected.
- Install, roll back, uninstall and switch between **stable** and **beta** per package.
- Only an owner or admin may do any of them.

These are available to developers through the Home API, not through a button. See [Developers](/docs/developers).

## 🙋 If a package misbehaves [#-if-a-package-misbehaves]

Open **Repairs** and check for an item. Then see [Troubleshooting](/docs/admin/look-after-it/troubleshooting-and-support-report).


# Reach Home when you are away (/docs/admin/connect-and-extend/remote-access)

{/* generated-source: backend/src/lib/tailscale.ts, backend/src/routes/tailscale.ts, frontend/src/apps/setup/AwayFromHome.tsx, backend/src/settings/networkKeys.ts */}

By default Home works only on your home Wi-Fi. To use it from anywhere, Home uses **Tailscale**, a free app that links your family's devices privately. Conversations go straight between the device and your Home computer. Tailscale sees device names and addresses, not what you say.

Home never turns this on by itself. Only an owner or admin can.

## ✅ Before you start [#-before-you-start]

1. Install Tailscale on the Home computer from tailscale.com/download.
2. Sign in to Tailscale with the account your family's devices will use.
3. Open Tailscale's DNS settings and turn on HTTPS certificates.

Pick a plain computer name first. Turning this on publishes the computer's Tailscale name in public certificate logs, so do not use a family name. Headscale is not supported by this flow.

## ✍️ Turn it on [#️-turn-it-on]

1. Open **Settings**, then **Home settings**, then **Network and access**.
2. Under **Reach Home from anywhere**, wait until the three lines say Ready.
3. Press **Turn on**.
4. Home shows a secure address and a QR code.

If a line is not ready, the **Turn on** button stays grey. If Tailscale is not signed in or HTTPS certificates are off, Home says "Sign in to Tailscale and enable HTTPS certificates first." Fix that in Tailscale, return to Home and try again.

## 📱 Add a phone or tablet [#-add-a-phone-or-tablet]

1. Install Tailscale on the device.
2. Sign in with the same account.
3. Scan the QR code, or open the address.

The address works only on devices signed in to your Tailscale account.

## 🔧 Related settings [#-related-settings]

| Setting | Default | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| **Away access through Tailscale** | Off | Set when you turn this on. |
| **Who can reach Home** | LAN | Loopback keeps Home on this computer. LAN lets devices on your home network connect. Needs a restart. |
| **Home network port** | 3000 | The port Home listens on. Changing it changes the address devices use. |
| **Reach the engine computer when away from home** | Off | For a separate engine computer. See [Use another computer for the AI](/docs/admin/install-and-set-up/use-another-computer-for-the-ai). |

## 🔐 Privacy [#-privacy]

Tailscale and the certificate authority are the two outside services involved. Both appear on the [privacy page](/docs/admin/look-after-it/privacy-audit), and only after you opt in.

Planned, not in the app yet: turning remote access on from the setup wizard. The wizard shows "Set up later", and you finish here.


# Set up web search (/docs/admin/connect-and-extend/web-search)

Home answers most questions from the model and its offline reference library. When a question needs fresh facts, Home can search the web. Web search is off until you set it up.

<Shot id="settings-search" />

## 📚 Library or internet [#-library-or-internet]

Under **Settings**, **Home settings**, **Search**, pick **Search sources**:

| Choice | What Home does |
|---|---|
| **Library first** (default) | Checks the offline library, goes online only if it has no answer. |
| **Internet first** | Goes online even when the library has a match. |
| **Library only** | Turns off the live Wikipedia-style lookup. Web search stays on unless it is also set to Library only. |

**Encyclopedia lookups** and **Web searches** (advanced) can each follow the household choice or override it. Children and teens keep their protections in every mode.

## 🔍 Connect SearXNG [#-connect-searxng]

SearXNG is a search service you run yourself. Home asks it for results, so no search company sees who asked.

1. Run SearXNG on a computer in your home. Turn on its JSON output.
2. Open **Settings**, **Home settings**, **Search**.
3. Type its address in **Your own SearXNG (optional)**, for example `http://192.0.2.20:8080`.
4. Ask Home something recent in **Chat**. A sources list appears under the reply.

Until an address is set, Home says "Web search isn't set up yet". Library and Wikipedia lookups still work.

Home checks SearXNG every hour while it is healthy and every 15 minutes while it is not. A failing check appears under **Repairs**, with the step to take. Check the computer is on, the address is right and JSON output is enabled.

## 🦆 Other sources [#-other-sources]

| Source | Who gets it | How to enable |
|---|---|---|
| **DuckDuckGo** | Adults only | Start the ddgs helper on the same computer, set `MAIPAI_DDGS_URL` to its loopback address, then pick it in **Web search sources**. |
| **Brave Search** | Adults only | Paste a key in **Brave Search key (optional)**. The words an adult searches go to Brave. The key is stored encrypted. |

Without the helper, Home says "DuckDuckGo search is not set up. Start the ddgs sidecar and set MAIPAI_DDGS_URL, or pick another web search source." A child's or teen's search never goes to either.

## 🛡️ Safe search [#️-safe-search]

| Setting | Behavior |
|---|---|
| **Safe search level** | **Default** follows age: strict for a child, moderate for a teen, off for an adult. A child's is always strict. |
| **Web search with child controls** | On: strictest SafeSearch, adult sites blocked, links hidden. Off: offline library only. |
| **Web search with teen controls** | On: moderate or stricter. |
| **Page text check** | Cleans fetched page text before the assistant reads it. On for children and teens. |

For site lists, see [Blocked-site lists](/docs/admin/people-and-safety/blocked-sites-and-news-feeds). For exactly what leaves the house, see [Privacy audit](/docs/admin/look-after-it/privacy-audit). To use search from a phone away from home, see [Remote access](/docs/admin/connect-and-extend/remote-access).


# How MaiPai Home works (/docs/admin/how-it-works/how-home-works)

MaiPai Home is one program that runs on a computer in your house. People reach it from a browser on a phone, tablet or laptop on your home Wi-Fi. Nothing goes through a MaiPai server, because there is none.

## 🗺️ The parts [#️-the-parts]

```
 Phone, tablet, laptop (browser)
            |
            |  your home network
            v
 +-------------------------------+        +---------------------------+
 | MaiPai Home (the hub)         |        | MaiPai Stack (the engine) |
 | people, memory, chat, settings| -----> | runs the AI models        |
 | packages, backups, updates    |        | same computer, or another |
 | stores: the data folder       |        | stores: models, engines   |
 +-------------------------------+        +---------------------------+
            |
            |  only what you allow
            v
   The internet (see Privacy audit)
```

| Part | What it does | Where it runs |
|---|---|---|
| **Home (the hub)** | Holds people, memories, conversations, settings, backups and the screens everyone uses. | The computer you installed it on. |
| **Stack (the engine)** | Runs the AI models for chat, listening, speaking and pictures. | The same computer, or a second one. See [Use another computer for the AI](/docs/admin/install-and-set-up/use-another-computer-for-the-ai). |
| **Packages** | Small features such as weather, timers and news. Home ships a default set. | Inside Home. |
| **Robot** | An optional companion body that pairs with Home. | Its own hardware. |

## 🔁 What happens when someone asks a question [#-what-happens-when-someone-asks-a-question]

1. The person types or speaks in the browser.
2. Home checks who they are and what their role allows.
3. Home builds the request and sends it to the engine.
4. The engine answers. Home checks the reply against the person's age band before showing it.
5. Home stores the conversation in its own folder.

If the engine is unreachable, chat pauses and Repairs shows why. Nothing is sent elsewhere as a fallback.

## 🏠 What this means for you [#-what-this-means-for-you]

- Your household's data stays in one folder you can back up. See [Where your data lives](/docs/admin/how-it-works/where-your-data-lives).
- Safety is built into Home, not into a package. Child protections cannot be removed. See [Safety settings](/docs/admin/people-and-safety/safety-settings).
- Home does not phone home. Every outbound connection is listed on the Privacy page. See [Privacy audit](/docs/admin/look-after-it/privacy-audit).

## 🧭 Where things are in the app [#-where-things-are-in-the-app]

The main menu has **Home**, **Chat**, **Family**, **Privacy** and **Settings**. Admin work lives under **Settings**, in the **Home settings** area. Backups, Updates, Repairs, Status, Storage and Engines are pages you reach from Settings.

<Callout type="info">The sidebar in some screenshots still says People. That page is now called Family.</Callout>


# People, roles and permissions (/docs/admin/how-it-works/people-roles-and-permissions)

{/* generated-source: frontend/src/apps/people/roles.ts, backend/src/lib/access.ts, backend/src/lib/personLifecycle.ts, shared/personCredentialRoles.ts */}

Every person in Home has one role. The role decides what they can open, change and see.

<Shot id="roles-users" />

## 🪜 The six roles [#-the-six-roles]

From most to least control: **owner**, **admin**, **adult**, **teen**, **child**, **guest**.

| Role | Sign-in | Runs the house | Reads others' private data |
|---|---|---|---|
| Owner | PIN or password | Everything, including restore | Own, plus a child's |
| Admin | PIN or password | Settings, people, backups, updates | Own, plus a child's |
| Adult | PIN or password | No | Own only |
| Teen | None required | No | Own only |
| Child | None required | No | Own only; a parent sees it |
| Guest | None required | No | None |

## 🔑 What only the owner can do [#-what-only-the-owner-can-do]

- Create another owner or an admin. An admin can add adults, teens, children and guests.
- Change a person's role. Nobody can change their own role.
- Restore a backup. An admin can see the backup list and run one.

Home refuses to remove or demote the household's only owner. Make someone else an owner first.

## 🛡️ What admins cannot see [#️-what-admins-cannot-see]

An owner or admin can open a **child's** profile, memories and settings. A **teen's** profile does not open at all for them, from Family or by typing its address. They cannot see another adult's memories or settings. A teen's chats and settings stay private from admins. This is built in and has no switch.

Household-wide switches still apply to every teen, such as **Web search with teen controls** under Settings, Search. Those change what Home does for teens as a group. They never show an admin what a teen asked.

## 🔒 Settings that follow the role [#-settings-that-follow-the-role]

- **Household settings** are writable only by an owner or admin.
- **Session lock** (ask for the PIN again after idle time) is set by an owner or admin, from the people list in Settings, Users.
- A child's **Sensitive subjects** levels are set only by an owner or admin. The child cannot change them.
- Each person's own look, voice and notification settings belong to that person.

## 🧪 Check it yourself [#-check-it-yourself]

1. Open **Family** as the admin.
2. Open a child's card. You see **Overview**, **Memories**, **Limits** and **Topics**.
3. Look at a teen's card in **Family**. It is not a link, and a typed address shows a "You cannot open this profile" message, so there is no **Limits**, **Topics** or **Memories** tab and no teen chats or memories are shown.

For what each role sees day to day, see [What each role can do](/docs/user/your-family/what-each-role-can-do).


# Where your data lives (/docs/admin/how-it-works/where-your-data-lives)

{/* generated-source: backend/src/lib/dataClasses.ts, backend/src/lib/paths.ts, backend/src/lib/backup.ts, scripts/uninstall.sh */}

Home keeps everything in one **data folder**. The default is a folder named `data` at the top of the Home folder. Two backup folders sit beside it, not inside it.

## 📁 What is in each folder [#-what-is-in-each-folder]

| Folder | What it holds | Replaceable? |
|---|---|---|
| `records` (the data folder itself) | People, memories, conversations, settings in one database file | No. Back this up. |
| `keys` | Encryption keys for secrets and face prints | No. Keep on a disk that is always connected. |
| `people` | Each person's files | No |
| `voice/cloned` | Cloned voices | No |
| `projects` | Project files | No |
| `packages` | Package data | Mostly |
| `models`, `engines`, `sidecars` | Downloaded AI models, engines and helper programs | Yes, downloaded again |
| `reference` | The offline reference library | Yes, downloaded again |
| `lists` | Blocked-site lists | Yes |
| `voice/stt`, `voice/wakewords`, `vision/models` | Speech, wake-word and face recognition models | Yes |
| `logs`, `cache`, `favicons`, `answer-images`, `local-app`, `labels` | Logs, caches and runtime files | Yes |
| `backups` (beside the data folder) | Your encrypted backup files | See below |
| `received-backups` (beside the data folder) | Backups pushed by paired devices | Not yet used by the app UI |

Put `records` and `backups` on different disks. A backup on the same disk is no safer than the data it copies.

## 💾 What a backup covers [#-what-a-backup-covers]

Today a backup is an encrypted copy of the household database: people, memories, conversations and settings. It does not include models, engines, the reference library or people's uploaded files. Those are downloaded or copied again after a restore. See [Backups and restore](/docs/admin/look-after-it/backups-and-restore).

## 🧹 Move or remove [#-move-or-remove]

- The Storage page shows what each person uses and the caps.
- To change where a folder lives, there is no screen yet. Planned, not in the app yet: the data-location picker. The setup wizard says so too.
- To uninstall, run the uninstall script. It asks before it deletes anything, and every prompt defaults to keep. See [Install and start](/docs/admin/install-and-set-up/install-and-start).

## ⚠️ Before you delete a folder you do not recognise [#️-before-you-delete-a-folder-you-do-not-recognise]

A folder that looks stray may be live household data. Open it first and check what it holds. Never delete `records` or `keys` without a backup and the backup key.

# Choose hardware (/docs/admin/install-and-set-up/choose-hardware)

<Callout type="info" title="Pre-alpha">
Home does not publish minimum specs yet. This page gives what the code supports and the tool that tells you whether a model fits your computer. It lists no speed numbers.
</Callout>

## 🖥️ What the installer supports [#️-what-the-installer-supports]

| Item | Supported |
|---|---|
| Operating system | macOS and Linux. Windows has a separate installer script. |
| Chip | x64 and arm64 |
| Engine computer (a second machine for the AI) | Ubuntu Linux only |

Home itself is light. The AI models are the heavy part. They need memory (RAM, or video memory on a graphics card) and disk space. The AI models page says the models it lists are about 7 to 10 GB each.

## ✅ Check a model against your computer [#-check-a-model-against-your-computer]

The **fit check** answers "will this model run here" before you download anything.

<Shot id="fit-check" />

1. Open **Settings**, **Home settings**, **Engines and AI**, then **AI models**.
2. Each model shows a verdict:

| Verdict | Meaning |
|---|---|
| **Runs well on this computer** | The model fits in memory with room to spare. |
| **Runs, but slowly** | It fits, but expect long waits. |
| **Won't fit** | It needs more memory than the computer has. |
| **Can't tell yet** | Home cannot read the computer's memory or the model's size. |

3. To check a model that is not listed, paste a Hugging Face link in **Check a model**.

The fit check needs the Stack (the engine software) to be running. A memory meter shows what is free.

## 🧭 Pick a shape [#-pick-a-shape]

| Setup | Good when |
|---|---|
| One computer runs Home and the AI | You have a Mac or PC with enough memory for a model you like. |
| Home on a small computer, AI on a stronger one | The stronger machine is Ubuntu. See [Use another computer for the AI](/docs/admin/install-and-set-up/use-another-computer-for-the-ai). |

## 💽 Disk and backups [#-disk-and-backups]

Keep the data folder on a disk with room for models and engines, and put backups on a different disk. Home raises a Repairs item when free space on its own disk drops below 2 GB (a setting you can change). Per-person storage has no cap by default. See [Where your data lives](/docs/admin/how-it-works/where-your-data-lives).

## 📋 Not declared yet [#-not-declared-yet]

- Minimum RAM, disk and graphics card.
- A list of tested computers.
- Speed numbers for any model.

Until those exist, treat the fit check as the answer, and start with a smaller model.


# First-run setup (/docs/admin/install-and-set-up/first-run-setup)

The first time you open Home it starts a setup wizard. It has three phases: **Your computers**, **Away from home** and **Meet your Home**.

<Callout type="info" title="Pre-alpha">
Some wizard screens say plainly that a step is not built yet. Those are listed below so you know what to expect.
</Callout>

<Shot id="setup-wizard" />

## 🪜 The screens [#-the-screens]

| Screen | What it does | State |
|---|---|---|
| Welcome | Press **Set up my Home**. | Built |
| **Where should Home's AI run?** | Pick **This computer** or **Another computer**. | Built |
| Storage | Choose where the AI models are stored. | Not built. The wizard says a disk picker is not available. |
| Setup checks | Test the computer. | Not built. It says so. |
| Plan | Recommend models for your hardware. | Not built. The plan from the installer is recorded for later. |
| **Reach Home from anywhere** | Set up Tailscale. | Not built here. Press **Set up later**, then finish in Settings. |
| **Create your owner account** | Your name and a PIN or password. | Built |
| **Let Home recognise you** | Face enrollment. | Optional. **Do this later** works. |
| First greeting | Home says hello. | Not built |
| **Your Home is ready** | Save your backup key, then **Open my Home**. | Built |

## 👑 Create the owner [#-create-the-owner]

1. Type your name.
2. Type a PIN or password. The owner and admin roles need one. The screen has an **Owner or admin?** note explaining the difference.
3. Continue.

The owner can add everyone else, including admins. See [People, roles and permissions](/docs/admin/how-it-works/people-roles-and-permissions).

If Home was already set up, it says "Home is already set up. Sign in instead." If it cannot read its progress, it says "Home can't read its setup progress. Refresh this page. If it keeps happening, restart MaiPai Home on this computer or run the installer again."

## 🔑 Save the backup key [#-save-the-backup-key]

On the last screen, press **Download** or **Print** under **Save your backup key**. Keep it somewhere other than this computer. If this computer breaks, the key brings your backups back on a new one. See [Backups and restore](/docs/admin/look-after-it/backups-and-restore).

Then press **Open my Home**.

## 📝 After setup [#-after-setup]

The wizard says how many things are left. They are in the setup checklist on the Home screen, such as adding family, enabling away access and saving the backup key. Come back to them at your own pace.

1. Add your family: [Add people](/docs/admin/people-and-safety/add-people-and-parental-controls).
2. Connect search: [Set up web search](/docs/admin/connect-and-extend/web-search).
3. Check what leaves the house: [Privacy audit](/docs/admin/look-after-it/privacy-audit).

For what the wizard looks like to a first-time user, see [Your first minutes](/docs/user/start-here/your-first-minutes).


# Install and start Home (/docs/admin/install-and-set-up/install-and-start)

<Callout type="info" title="Pre-alpha">
Home has no packaged installer yet. It runs from source, and an installer script exists for a service install. Nothing is deployed to a real household yet.
</Callout>

## 🧰 What you need [#-what-you-need]

- macOS or Linux on x64 or arm64
- [Bun](https://bun.sh), the JavaScript runtime
- Git
- Internet for the first install

## ▶️ Run from source [#️-run-from-source]

1. Get the code.

```bash
git clone https://github.com/getmaipai/home.git
```

2. Go into the folder. Use the full path where you cloned it.

```bash
cd /Users/example/Developer/home
```

3. Install the packages.

```bash
bun install
```

4. Start Home.

```bash
bun start
```

Home builds, runs in the background and prints its addresses. Open the address Home prints. By default it is `http://localhost:3000`. The first person to sign in becomes the **owner**. Running `bun start` again prints the addresses without starting a second copy.

## ⏹️ Stop and restart [#️-stop-and-restart]

Run these in the same folder.

```bash
bun stop
```

```bash
bun restart
```

The log is `data/local-app/app.log`.

## 🛎️ Install as a service [#️-install-as-a-service]

The installer runs Home in the background so it survives a reboot with nobody signed in. For the short, step by step version for the household, see the [install, upgrade, uninstall and fix page](/docs/user/start-here/install-upgrade-uninstall).

1. Run the installer as root. It installs Home only and prints the address of the setup wizard. SSH works.

```bash
sudo bash /Users/example/Developer/home/scripts/install.sh
```

2. Open the address. In the wizard, choose where the AI runs. **This computer** makes Home install the MaiPai Stack right then, with a progress bar. **Another computer** installs no Stack here.

3. To see what it would do first, add `--dry-run`. `--stack-only` runs only the AI engine step, which is what the wizard starts; run it by hand if the wizard cannot.

| Item | macOS | Linux |
|---|---|---|
| Install folder | `/usr/local/maipai-home` | `/opt/maipai-home` |
| Home service | launchd daemon `com.maipai.home` | systemd unit `maipai-home.service` |
| Stack service | per-user LaunchAgent `com.maipai.stack`, started at login | systemd user unit, kept alive by lingering |
| Log trimming | daily launchd daemon `com.maipai.logrotate` | journald |
| Home logs | `data/logs/launchd.out.log`, `launchd.err.log` | `journalctl -u maipai-home` |
| Stack logs | `stack/data/logs/stack.log`, `stack.error.log` | `journalctl --user -u maipai-stack` |

### What it checks first [#what-it-checks-first]

- Required tools (`curl`, `tar`, `rsync`, `unzip`, `shasum`). On a Mac a miss points at `xcode-select --install`. Homebrew is never used, and Python is not needed.
- Free disk space: 3 GB for Home. The Stack step checks 6 GB more, and the wizard plan checks the models.
- For the Stack step only: a logged-in desktop session on macOS. Home itself needs none.
- The Bun runtime and the install checks, after the build and before any service starts.

### The Stack step [#the-stack-step]

`install.sh --stack-only` fetches, builds and starts the Stack, writes `engines.stack.url`, and records its progress in `data/stack-install.json` (state, stage, a plain problem). Home reads that file for the wizard bar. On macOS Home is a root daemon and runs the step itself. On Linux Home is an unprivileged user, so the installer adds a one-shot unit, `maipai-stack-install.service`, and a sudoers rule that allows exactly `systemctl start --no-block maipai-stack-install.service` for the Home user. The `scripts/` folder is root-owned so that user cannot change what the unit runs. The step is safe to run again.

### Ports [#ports]

Home uses `MAIPAI_PORT` (default 3000). The Stack uses `MAIPAI_STACK_PORT` (default 8770). If a port is taken, the installer takes the next free one. Both values are written into Home's service as `PORT` and `MAIPAI_STACK_PORT`, so the running app and the installer agree. An upgrade keeps the port the last install used. The installer, the service files, the health checks and the backend all read the names above (`backend/src/lib/ports.ts` on the app side).

### Release, plan and version [#release-plan-and-version]

The installer installs the **latest published release**, never the main branch. If no release exists it stops with "could not find a published release ... there is nothing to install". Run from source until one does. `--version v0.1.0` installs a named release. Choose a setup plan with `--plan recommended`, `--plan moderate` or `--plan minimal`; the wizard reads it later.

### Upgrade, resume and roll back [#upgrade-resume-and-roll-back]

Running it again upgrades in place. Order: stop Home and the Stack, save `data/` to `upgrade-backups/<time>-from-<tag>/data.tar.gz` (the last two are kept), replace the program files, rebuild, start, wait for Home (`/`) and the Stack (`/healthz`), then write `.installed-tag`. The Stack's `stack/data/` (models and settings) and the Bun runtime are never replaced.

An upgrade of an install that already has a Stack rebuilds the Stack too. A run that stopped part way is finished by running the same command again. It sees no `.installed-tag`, treats the folder as unfinished and continues. If a run fails after the old Home was stopped but before any file changed, Home is started again on the old version.

```bash
sudo bash /usr/local/maipai-home/scripts/install.sh --rollback
```

Rollback installs the tag in `.previous-tag`, moves the newer `data/` to `data.rolled-back-<time>` and restores the copy taken before that upgrade. The Stack's own data is not rolled back.

### After a restart [#after-a-restart]

Home starts at boot. The Stack is a per-user LaunchAgent, so it starts when that user logs in. Turn on automatic login for a Mac that restarts unattended. FileVault blocks automatic login; the installer prints a warning when FileVault is on.

### Gatekeeper [#gatekeeper]

The installer clears the quarantine flag on the install folder and checks the signature of Bun and the Stack binary. An unsigned binary gets an ad-hoc signature, which Apple silicon requires. If macOS still blocks one, choose Allow Anyway in System Settings, Privacy and Security.

## 🗑️ Uninstall [#️-uninstall]

```bash
sudo bash /Users/example/Developer/home/scripts/uninstall.sh
```

It stops and removes the Home service, the Stack service and the log trimming job, then asks whether to keep or wipe your data. The default on every prompt is keep, and a wipe needs you to type `DELETE MY DATA` exactly. A wipe covers `data/`, `backups/`, `received-backups/`, the Stack's data, `upgrade-backups/` and any `data.rolled-back-*` folder. Take a backup first. See [Backups and restore](/docs/admin/look-after-it/backups-and-restore).

## ➡️ Next [#️-next]

[First-run setup](/docs/admin/install-and-set-up/first-run-setup).


# Settings reference (/docs/admin/install-and-set-up/settings-reference)

{/* generated-source: backend/src/settings/*Keys.ts, commons/spec/settings/areas.json, commons/spec/settings/keys.json */}

<Callout type="info" title="How to read this page">
**Home** settings are set once for the household. **Person** settings belong to one person, and the guardian rules decide who may change them for a child or teen. Level is **basic**, **advanced** or **expert**; the app hides higher levels until asked. A blank "What it does" means the screen explains it in place. Settings marked "Not active yet" are saved but nothing reads them today. Robot and vision settings (keys starting `robot.`, `person.robot.`, `person.vision.` and `vision.`) are used by MaiPai Bot, not by Home itself.

One more setting, **Wake word listening** (`voice.wakeword.enabled`, device scope, default off), appears only when the wake-word files are installed, so it is not in the tables. Only owners, admins and adults see it. The one detector today is openWakeWord "Hey Jarvis", and it runs in the browser. No setup screen downloads the wake-word files; the setting stays hidden until all four are on disk in the `voice/wakewords` data folder (see [Where your data lives](/docs/admin/how-it-works/where-your-data-lives)).
</Callout>

Each table gives the label as shown, the key (useful in a support report), the default, the level and what it does. For the same screens in plain language, see the [user guide](/docs/user).


## Home settings [#home-settings]


### Home settings > Engines and AI > Chat card [#home-settings--engines-and-ai--chat-card]

| Setting | Key | Default | Level | What it does |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| **Chat context size override** | `chat.context_size_override` | 0 | advanced | 0 lets the hub pick the largest context that fits this computer's memory. A higher number can run out of memory; a lower one leaves headroom but remembers less of the conversation. |
| **Flash attention override** | `chat.flash_attention_override` | auto | advanced | "Auto" lets the hub decide based on the model and the quantized-KV-cache setting. Flash attention speeds up longer conversations; a very old GPU may not support it. |
| **KV cache precision override** | `chat.kv_cache_override` | auto | advanced | "Auto" quantizes the conversation cache to fit more context in the same memory, with a small quality tradeoff. "Full" uses full precision: more accurate, uses roughly twice the memory for the same context size. |
| **Selected chat model** | `chat.model_id` | empty | expert | The catalog model id currently downloaded and running for chat. Changed through the AI models page, not here. |
| **How a teen's replies are checked** | `chat.teen_gate_grain` | sentence | advanced | "Sentence" checks every sentence before a teen sees it (the default). "Arrival" shows a teen's reply as it is written and checks it as it comes, so part of a sentence can show before its check finishes and the reply stops there if the check fails. Children and anything spoken always check every sentence first. |
| **Chat model choice** | `engines.chat.choice` | auto | basic | Choose the model for the Chat role. Auto follows the selected setup plan. Only an admin can change this. |
| **Router model choice** | `engines.router.choice` | auto | basic | Choose the model for the Router role. Auto follows the selected setup plan. Only an admin can change this. |
| **Embed model choice** | `engines.embed.choice` | auto | basic | Choose the model for the Embed role. Auto follows the selected setup plan. Only an admin can change this. |
| **Rerank model choice** | `engines.rerank.choice` | auto | basic | Choose the model for the Rerank role. Auto follows the selected setup plan. Only an admin can change this. |
| **Vision model choice** | `engines.vision.choice` | auto | basic | Choose the model for the Vision role. Auto follows the selected setup plan. Only an admin can change this. |
| **Image model choice** | `engines.image.choice` | auto | basic | Choose the model for the Image role. Auto follows the selected setup plan. Only an admin can change this. |
| **Video model choice** | `engines.video.choice` | auto | basic | Choose the model for the Video role. Auto follows the selected setup plan. Only an admin can change this. |
| **Music model choice** | `engines.music.choice` | auto | basic | Choose the model for the Music role. Auto follows the selected setup plan. Only an admin can change this. |
| **Coding model choice** | `engines.coding.choice` | auto | basic | Choose the model for the Coding role. Auto follows the selected setup plan. Only an admin can change this. |
| **Judge model choice** | `engines.judge.choice` | auto | basic | Choose the model for the Judge role. Auto follows the selected setup plan. Only an admin can change this. |
| **Tts model choice** | `engines.tts.choice` | auto | basic | Choose the model for the Tts role. Auto follows the selected setup plan. Only an admin can change this. |
| **Stt model choice** | `engines.stt.choice` | auto | basic | Choose the model for the Stt role. Auto follows the selected setup plan. Only an admin can change this. |
| **Wakeword model choice** | `engines.wakeword.choice` | auto | basic | Choose the model for the Wakeword role. Auto follows the selected setup plan. Only an admin can change this. |
| **Turn Signal model choice** | `engines.turn_signal.choice` | auto | basic | Choose the model for the Turn Signal role. Auto follows the selected setup plan. Only an admin can change this. |
| **Reach the engine computer when away from home** | `engines.stack.remote.allow_tailnet` | off | advanced | Off, Home reaches the engine computer only from inside your home network. On, Home may also reach it through your private tailnet when you are away. Turn it on only if you have joined both computers to your tailnet yourself. Only an admin can change this. Shown only while the engine runs on another computer. |
| **Engine computer name** | `engines.stack.remote.host` | empty | basic | The name of the computer that runs the engine, the way your network knows it. Only an admin can change this. Shown only while the engine runs on another computer. |
| **Engine computer local port** | `engines.stack.remote.local_port` | 8771 | advanced | The port on this computer where the engine computer's connection appears. Change it only if another program already uses it. Only an admin can change this. Shown only while the engine runs on another computer. |
| **Engine computer secure connection port** | `engines.stack.remote.ssh_port` | 22 | advanced | The port Home uses to open its secure connection to the engine computer. Leave it at 22 unless that computer was set up differently. Only an admin can change this. Shown only while the engine runs on another computer. |
| **MaiPai Stack address** | `engines.stack.url` | empty | expert | Empty uses Home's own built-in engines. With the engine on this computer, set this to the address of the MaiPai Stack installed here to route chat, embeddings and voice through it. With the engine on another computer, Home fills this in for you from the connection settings, so leave it empty. Only an admin can change this. |
| **Help the chat remember to search the web** | `chat.search_assist` | shadow | advanced | "Off" is the kill switch: nothing is scored. "Shadow" (the default) only counts, as a number, how often a web search looked needed, and changes no reply. "Rescue" is not active yet; for now it behaves like shadow. Children and teens are never scored. |
| **Use the MaiPai Stack for chat** | `engines.stack.use_chat` | off | expert | Deprecated, ignored. A configured Stack serves every role. |
| **Use the MaiPai Stack for search (embeddings)** | `engines.stack.use_embeddings` | off | expert | Deprecated, ignored. A configured Stack serves every role. |
| **Use the MaiPai Stack for listening (speech to text)** | `engines.stack.use_stt` | off | expert | Deprecated, ignored. A configured Stack serves every role. |
| **Use the MaiPai Stack for speaking (text to speech)** | `engines.stack.use_tts` | off | expert | Deprecated, ignored. A configured Stack serves every role. |
| **Where the engine runs** | `engines.stack.where` | this_computer | basic | "This computer" runs the engine on the machine Home is installed on. "Another computer" runs it on a different computer in your home that you reach over your network. Only an admin can change this. |
| **Hugging Face token (for voice cloning)** | `voice.hf_token` | empty | advanced | Needed to clone a voice from a recording. Accept the terms at huggingface.co/kyutai/pocket-tts, then create a read token at huggingface.co/settings/tokens and paste it here. |

### Home settings > Search > Blocked sites [#home-settings--search--blocked-sites]

| Setting | Key | Default | Level | What it does |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| **Blocked sites with child controls** | `search.blocklists.child` | ["blp-gambling", "blp-scam", "blp-phishi | advanced | Which lists of blocked sites are checked when MaiPai searches the web for people using child controls. Adult sites are always blocked for child and teen controls and are not listed here. Home downloads each list once and keeps it up to date. Web search for child controls starts once every list checked here has been downloaded. Only an admin can change this. |
| **Blocked sites with teen controls** | `search.blocklists.teen` | ["blp-gambling", "blp-scam", "blp-phishi | advanced | Which lists of blocked sites are checked when MaiPai searches the web for people using teen controls. Adult sites are always blocked for child and teen controls and are not listed here. Web search for teen controls starts once every list checked here has been downloaded. Only an admin can change this. It does not show anyone what a teen searched for or which sites were blocked. |
| **Blocked sites with adult controls** | `search.blocklists.adult` | [] | advanced | Lists of blocked sites to check when MaiPai searches the web for adults. None are checked unless you pick them. Scam, phishing and malware lists are a good start for a household that wants that protection. Only an admin can change this. |
| **Kinds of sites to block** | `search.blocklists` | [] | advanced | Kinds of sites that web search, page reads and answer pictures leave out. Kids, Teens and Adults each start from their own user defaults. The global defaults add kinds for everyone, and a user override adds or removes kinds for one person. The adult-site list is always on for a child or teen and no override can turn it off. Only an admin can change this, and it never shows what anyone searched for. |
| **Always block these sites** | `search.hosts.deny` | empty | advanced | Sites that web search never shows for anyone, separated by commas, like example.com. A site you list here also blocks its subpages. This works for every age, and it always wins over the allowed list. Only an admin can change this. |
| **Allow these sites** | `search.hosts.allow` | empty | advanced | Sites that web search may show even when a blocked-sites list has them, separated by commas, like example.com. It cannot allow an adult site for child or teen controls, and it cannot allow a site you list under Always block these sites. Only an admin can change this. |
| **Always block these sites for child** | `search.hosts.child.deny` | empty | advanced | Sites that web search never shows to a child, separated by commas, like example.com, on top of the household list. A site you list here also blocks its subpages. It always wins over the allowed lists. Only an admin can change this. |
| **Allow these sites for child** | `search.hosts.child.allow` | empty | advanced | Sites that web search may show to a child even when a blocked-sites list has them, separated by commas, like example.com, on top of the household list. It cannot allow an adult site for child or teen controls, and it cannot allow a site that is in an always-block list. Only an admin can change this. |
| **Always block these sites for teen** | `search.hosts.teen.deny` | empty | advanced | Sites that web search never shows to a teen, separated by commas, like example.com, on top of the household list. A site you list here also blocks its subpages. It always wins over the allowed lists. Only an admin can change this. |
| **Allow these sites for teen** | `search.hosts.teen.allow` | empty | advanced | Sites that web search may show to a teen even when a blocked-sites list has them, separated by commas, like example.com, on top of the household list. It cannot allow an adult site for child or teen controls, and it cannot allow a site that is in an always-block list. Only an admin can change this. |
| **Always block these sites for adult** | `search.hosts.adult.deny` | empty | advanced | Sites that web search never shows to an adult, separated by commas, like example.com, on top of the household list. A site you list here also blocks its subpages. It always wins over the allowed lists. Only an admin can change this. |
| **Allow these sites for adult** | `search.hosts.adult.allow` | empty | advanced | Sites that web search may show to an adult even when a blocked-sites list has them, separated by commas, like example.com, on top of the household list. It cannot allow an adult site for child or teen controls, and it cannot allow a site that is in an always-block list. Only an admin can change this. |

### Home settings > Network and access > Network [#home-settings--network-and-access--network]

<Shot id="settings-network" />

| Setting | Key | Default | Level | What it does |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| **Home network port** | `network.hub_port` | 3000 | expert | The port Home listens on. Changing it needs a restart and changes the address devices use. Only an admin can change this. |
| **Who can reach Home** | `network.lan_exposure` | lan | advanced | Loopback keeps Home on this computer. LAN lets devices on your home network connect. Changing this needs a restart. Only an admin can change this. |
| **Away access through Tailscale** | `network.tailnet_access` | off | basic | Lets your devices reach Home through your private Tailscale network. Tailscale sees device names and addresses, not your conversations. Home never turns this on for you. Only an admin can change this. |

A list unchecked for every user type is switched off. Only an admin can change this. |

### Home settings > Search > Web search [#home-settings--search--web-search]

| Setting | Key | Default | Level | What it does |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| **Look up words online** | `search.dictionary_fallback` | off | advanced | Look up a word online when the library does not have it. The word you ask about is sent to Wiktionary (Wikimedia). Adults only. Off by default. |
| **Search fetch cache limit (GB)** | `search.fetch_cache_gb` | 2 | advanced | Maximum disk space used for cached search pages. The default is 2 GB on p16 and 10 GB on p64 and p128. |
| **Your own SearXNG (optional)** | `search.searxng_url` | empty | advanced | Your own SearXNG (optional). Leave empty to use the search service MaiPai runs for you. |
| **Search sources** | `search.source_mode` | mix | basic | Where MaiPai looks for answers: Internet first, Library only, or Library first (the recommended choice). Library only turns off just the live Wikipedia-style lookup; web search stays on unless web search is itself set to Library only. Children and teens keep their current protections in every mode, and this choice never widens what they can reach. |
| **Encyclopedia lookups** | `search.source_mode.wikimedia` | inherit | advanced | Gives the live Wikipedia-style lookup its own choice. Same as the household choice follows the search sources setting. Library only turns this lookup off. Children and teens never use this lookup in any mode. |
| **Web searches** | `search.source_mode.web` | inherit | advanced | Gives web search its own choice. Same as the household choice follows the search sources setting. Library only here turns off web search, link reading, Wayback and the hosted search provider together. Children and teens keep their current protections in every mode. |
| **Web search with child controls** | `search.web.child_mode` | on | basic | When this is on, MaiPai can look things up on the web for people using child controls. Results go through SafeSearch at its strictest, adult sites are blocked, and links are hidden. When it is off, answers come only from the offline library. Only an admin can change this, and a child's searches show in that child's own chats. |
| **Web search with teen controls** | `search.web.teen_mode` | on | basic | When this is on, MaiPai can look things up on the web for people using teen controls. Results go through SafeSearch at moderate or stricter, and adult sites are blocked. When it is off, answers come only from the offline library. Only an admin can change this. It does not show anyone what a teen searched for. |
| **Web search sources** | `search.web_sources` | ["searxng"] | advanced | Which services answer web searches. SearXNG, the household's own search service, is on by default. DuckDuckGo is not available yet. With more than one picked, their results are blended into one list. Children and teens only use SearXNG. To turn web search off, set Web searches to Library only. Pictures and videos always use SearXNG. |
| **Use archived pages when a source is missing** | `search.wayback_fallback` | on | advanced | Check the Wayback Machine when a cited page returns not found. |
| **Brave Search key (optional)** | `search.brave_api_key` | empty | advanced | Optional. Search works without any key. If you add a Brave Search API key, an adult's web searches go to Brave Search instead of your SearXNG, so the words searched leave your house. A child's or teen's searches never do. The key is stored encrypted and can't be read back. Clear it to go back to keyless search. |

### Home settings > General > Internet check [#home-settings--general--internet-check]

| Setting | Key | Default | Level | What it does |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| **Internet check name** | `status.internet_probe.dns_name` | example.com | advanced | The name MaiPai looks up once a minute to check whether internet name lookups work. |
| **Check whether the internet is reachable** | `status.internet_probe.enabled` | on | basic | Once a minute, MaiPai looks up a neutral name and opens an empty connection to the chosen address. Turn this off to stop those checks. |
| **Internet check address** | `status.internet_probe.tcp_address` | 1.1.1.1 | advanced | The public IP address MaiPai connects to once a minute without sending data. |
| **Internet check port** | `status.internet_probe.tcp_port` | 443 | advanced | The port MaiPai opens and immediately closes without sending data. |

| **Default per-person storage cap (bytes)** | `storage.person.default_cap_bytes` | 21474836480 | basic | How many bytes each person may use for their own files, unless that person has their own override below. |

# Use another computer for the AI (/docs/admin/install-and-set-up/use-another-computer-for-the-ai)

Home can use the AI engines (the Stack) on the same computer, or on a second computer in your home. A second computer is useful when it has a stronger graphics card or more memory than the one running Home.

<Shot id="settings-engines" />

## ✅ Before you start [#-before-you-start]

- The second computer runs Ubuntu Linux. Other systems are not supported for this.
- Both computers are on the same home network.
- You can use `sudo` on the engine computer.

## 🔧 Set up the engine computer [#-set-up-the-engine-computer]

1. On the engine computer, run the installer with the engine option.

```bash
sudo bash /home/example/home/scripts/install.sh --engine-computer
```

The installer creates a `maipai-stack` service user, installs the Stack under `/opt/maipai-stack`, keeps its data in `/data/stack`, and enables SSH, asking first if `openssh-server` is missing. It then installs the `maipai-engine` tool.

2. Wait for "Ready to pair."

## 🔗 Pair it with Home [#-pair-it-with-home]

1. In Home, open **Settings**, **Home settings**, **Engines and AI**.
2. Press **Pair engine computer**.
3. Pick **Another computer**, then **Next**.
4. Type the engine computer's name or home network address, for example `192.0.2.20`, and its SSH port (usually 22).
5. Press **Get a one-time code**. Home shows a command like `sudo maipai-engine pair https://home.example ABCD-EFGH-JKLM`. Copy it.
6. Run that command on the engine computer. The code works once and Home shows when it expires. The command prints a **check code**.
7. Back in Home, press **Check the engine computer**, type the check code, then press **Pin this computer**.

Home reads the computer's security key and compares the check code, so you know you are talking to your machine and not another one.

Home runs a hop-by-hop connection test and shows **PASS** or **FAIL** for each hop with the fix.

## 🩺 Check it later [#-check-it-later]

- **Engines** shows **Engine health** and a **Check the connection** button.
- On the engine computer, `sudo maipai-engine status` and `sudo maipai-engine doctor` report what is running.
- **Needs restart** or **Update available** on a row means exactly that.

## ✂️ Unpair [#️-unpair]

1. On the engine computer, run `sudo maipai-engine unpair`.
2. In Home, press **Revoke link key**.

## 🌍 Away from home [#-away-from-home]

Reaching the engine computer through Tailscale is off by default. Turn on the `engines.stack.remote.allow_tailnet` setting only after you have joined both computers to your Tailscale network yourself. See [Remote access](/docs/admin/connect-and-extend/remote-access).

## 🔧 If chat stops answering [#-if-chat-stops-answering]

**Engines** says "No Stack configured" when no engine is set. Open **Where the engine runs**, pick one, and run **Check the connection**. The page for the Home computer is at [Troubleshooting](/docs/admin/look-after-it/troubleshooting-and-support-report).


# Backups and restore (/docs/admin/look-after-it/backups-and-restore)

{/* generated-source: backend/src/lib/backup.ts, backend/src/lib/restoreStaging.ts, backend/src/lib/emergencyKit.ts, backend/src/lib/backupTargets.ts, backend/src/routes/backups.ts, frontend/src/shell/pages/BackupsPage.tsx */}

A backup is one encrypted copy of Home's household database: people, memories, conversations and settings. Models, engines, the reference library and uploaded files are not in it. Those are downloaded or copied again after a restore.

<Shot id="backups" />

## ⏰ What happens on its own [#-what-happens-on-its-own]

- Home takes a backup **every day**.
- It keeps **7 daily**, **4 weekly** and **3 monthly** copies, and deletes older ones.
- **Backup storage limit (GB)** under Storage and backups is 0 by default, which means no limit. Set a number and Home deletes the oldest first to stay under it.
- Backups go in the `backups` folder beside the data folder. Files are named `backup-<time>-<suffix>.db.enc`.

A backup on the same disk as Home does not survive that disk failing. Copy the `backups` folder to another disk or computer regularly.

## 🔑 Save your backup key [#-save-your-backup-key]

Backups are encrypted. The **backup key** is what lets a new computer read them. The setup wizard offers **Save your backup key** at the end, with **Download** and **Print**. The file is `maipai-home-emergency-backup-key.txt`. Saving the key later from **Settings**, **Backups** gives the same file name.

Keep it somewhere other than the Home computer, such as a password manager or a printed page in a drawer. Without it, a restore on a new computer cannot read the backups.

If Home fails to make the key, it says "Home couldn't make your backup key. Press Download again." If it fails again, open Repairs.

## 💾 Back up now [#-back-up-now]

1. Open **Settings**, then **Home settings**, then **Storage and backups**, then **Backups**.
2. Press **Back up now**.
3. The new copy appears in the table with its date and size.

Owners and admins can do this. A new household shows "No backups yet." until the first run.

## ♻️ Restore [#️-restore]

Only the owner can restore.

1. Open **Backups**.
2. Press **Restore** on the row you want and confirm.
3. A **Ready to restore** banner appears. Restart Home.
4. At the next start Home swaps in the restored database.

Before it swaps, Home takes a fresh backup and checks the archive. If the file cannot be read, Home says "that backup could not be read. Try another one." Press **Cancel restore** on the banner to change your mind before restarting.

The database you replaced is kept as `hub.db.pre-restore`. Keep it until you are sure the restore is right.

## 🗄️ A second copy [#️-a-second-copy]

Home can also copy backups to a mounted folder, such as a NAS share. Planned, not in the app yet: a screen for it. Today the folder is set through the Home API by an owner or admin. If that copy starts failing, Home raises a **Repairs** item and can message you on Telegram. See [Notifications and Telegram](/docs/admin/connect-and-extend/notifications-and-telegram).

## 🧪 Practice [#-practice]

A restore you have never tried is a guess. Once, on a spare computer, install Home, restore a backup with your saved key and sign in.


# Devices and signed-in sessions (/docs/admin/look-after-it/devices-and-sessions)

This page shows your own devices and sessions. It is not a household list.

## ✍️ Steps [#️-steps]

1. Open **Settings**, **Data and privacy**, then **Signed-in devices**.
2. Under **Devices** you see paired robots, pods, TVs, phones, desktops and browsers, with the room and when each was last seen. A device that never connected says "never connected".
3. Tap **Remove** beside one, then **Yes, remove it**. It must be paired again to reconnect. **Keep it** cancels.
4. Under **Signed-in sessions**, tap **Sign out** beside another browser, then **Yes, sign it out**.

Your current session shows **This device** and has no sign-out button. Use **Log out** in the profile menu for that.

If nothing is paired, you see "No devices paired to your profile yet."

## 🙋 Still need help? [#-still-need-help]

If a list will not load, reload the page. If it keeps failing, see [Troubleshooting and support report](/docs/admin/look-after-it/troubleshooting-and-support-report).


# Performance (/docs/admin/look-after-it/performance)

This page is for owners and admins. Other roles are refused.

## ✍️ Steps [#️-steps]

1. Open **Settings**, **Home settings**, **Maintenance**, then **Performance**.
2. Read the cards:

| Card | What it shows |
|---|---|
| **Reply time per day** | How long replies took each day. |
| **Queues** | Waiting work: **Memory judge**, **Embedding retry**, **Ingestion**. |
| **Turns per engine** | Which engine answered. |
| **Route taken** | Which path each turn followed. |
| **Layers** | Time spent in each step of a turn. |
| **Label harvest** | How many turns were counted in the window. |
| **Engines** | Engine health. |
| **Storage & hardware** | Disk and computer details. |

The numbers come from what Home already records. Nothing new is collected, and nothing leaves the house.

**Layers** says "No traced turns yet" until a turn has left a timing trace.

If the page fails, it says "Could not load performance." Reload it. See [Troubleshooting](/docs/admin/look-after-it/troubleshooting-and-support-report).

## 🙋 Still need help? [#-still-need-help]

If a queue keeps growing, open **Status** in **Maintenance** and check the engines.


# Privacy audit (/docs/admin/look-after-it/privacy-audit)

{/* generated-source: backend/src/lib/privacy.ts, backend/src/routes/privacy.ts, backend/packages manifests (data_sources) */}

Home runs in your house. Nothing leaves unless a row on this page says so. Open it at **Settings**, **Home settings**, **Privacy**, **What connects to the internet**, or **Settings**, **Data and privacy** for your own view.

The page is built from the code and each package's declared sources, so it cannot drift from what Home does. A row shows only while that feature is in use.

## 🌍 What can leave the house [#-what-can-leave-the-house]

| Row | When | What goes |
|---|---|---|
| Model downloads (wake word, face, speech, robot) | Once per model, the first time a feature needs it. For the wake word, that is the first time someone switches it on in chat. | A download request |
| Update check (GitHub) | At most once a day | Your internet address |
| Blocked-site index and lists | Index about daily, lists about monthly | Your internet address. Shown only while a list is on. |
| Internet check | Once a minute | A DNS lookup of example.com and an empty connection to 1.1.1.1:443. Turn it off under **Internet check**. |
| News feeds | About every 30 minutes at most, while the shelf is on | A plain request for the feed file |
| Reference books (Kiwix) | When an adult installs or updates one | A download request |
| Answer pictures (Wikipedia, Wikidata) | When a picture is picked for an answer | A request for the picture |
| Voice list | When an adult opens the list of voices | A request for the list |
| DuckDuckGo | Adult web search, only if picked | The search words |
| Brave | Adult web search, only with a key | The search words |
| Telegram | When a notification you chose fires | The notification text |
| Tailscale and Let's Encrypt | Only after an owner turns on away access, and at renewal | Device names, the computer's name |

A child's or teen's search words never go to DuckDuckGo or Brave.

## 🏠 What stays on your network [#-what-stays-on-your-network]

| Row | Destination |
|---|---|
| Home Assistant | Your own Home Assistant on your LAN |
| Robot connection addresses | A paired robot asking Home for addresses |
| API token | Only if an adult creates a token and gives it to another app |
| Engine computer | Your engine computer, when someone chats or asks for a picture. Through Tailscale when you are away. |

## ✅ How to check it yourself [#-how-to-check-it-yourself]

1. Open the page and read each row's destination.
2. Confirm every destination is one you expect.
3. To turn something off: the internet check under **Internet check**, the news shelf under **News shelf**, Telegram by clearing the token, DuckDuckGo by unpicking it, Brave by clearing its key, away access under **Network and access**.
4. Look again. The row is gone when the feature is off.

Package data sources appear here too, with the destination, when, what and who. For how privacy works in plain words, see [What never leaves](/docs/user/privacy-and-safety/what-never-leaves).

There is no row for MaiPai itself. Home has no MaiPai-run service in your data path.


# Troubleshooting and support report (/docs/admin/look-after-it/troubleshooting-and-support-report)

<Shot id="repairs" />

## 🛠️ Repairs [#️-repairs]

Open **Settings**, **Home settings**, **Maintenance**, then **Repairs**. Home lists problems it found, such as web search failing, a backup copy failing or an engine reporting trouble. Each item may have a fix button, named for what it does, and has a **Dismiss** button.

- The fix button runs the repair Home offers. Not every item has one.
- **Dismiss** asks you to confirm, then hides the item.

Only an owner or admin can fix or dismiss. If a button fails, Home says "Could not fix that repair." or "Could not dismiss that repair." Reload the page and try again. If the list does not load, it says "Could not load repairs." Check Home is running and that you are signed in as an owner or admin.

Tick **Telegram me about new Repairs items** to hear about them when you are out.

## 🩺 Other places to look [#-other-places-to-look]

| Page | Use it for |
|---|---|
| **Status** (Maintenance) | Whether Home, the engines and the internet check are working. |
| **Performance** (Maintenance) | How busy the computer is. |
| **Engines** | Engine health, and **Check the connection** to a separate engine computer. |
| **Storage** | Free disk space. Home warns when free space drops below 2 GB. |
| `data/local-app/app.log` | The log when you run from source. |

## 🧰 Common fixes [#-common-fixes]

| Symptom | Do this |
|---|---|
| Chat does not answer | Open **Engines**. If it says "No Stack configured", set the engine location. See [Use another computer for the AI](/docs/admin/install-and-set-up/use-another-computer-for-the-ai). |
| Web search says it is not set up | Add a SearXNG address. See [Set up web search](/docs/admin/connect-and-extend/web-search). |
| Phone cannot reach Home | See [Reach Home when you are away](/docs/admin/connect-and-extend/remote-access). |
| Someone cannot sign in | See [Cannot sign in](/docs/user/fix-a-problem/cannot-sign-in). |

## 📄 Support report [#-support-report]

Home can build a redacted report for you to attach when you ask for help. Open `/api/storage/diagnostics` while signed in as an owner or admin. It returns:

- Home's instance id, never the household's name.
- People: id, role, whether enabled, where they came from and when created. No names.
- Issue source, key, severity and times. No titles or details.
- Package ids, status and smoke test results.
- Household settings, without secrets.
- A storage summary.

It never contains conversations, memories, files or names. Read it before you send it.

Planned, not in the app yet: a **Create a report** button.


# Read a turn trace (/docs/admin/look-after-it/turn-trace)

This page is for owners and admins.

## ✍️ Steps [#️-steps]

1. In Chat, find the reply you want to look at and tap the **More** (three dots) button under it.
2. Tap **Turn trace**.
3. Read the **Turn trace** page. The **Trace** card lists each step as a bar, with the total time in milliseconds.

Steps include the pipeline stages, **Model generation** and **Tool call**. Each can be completed, failed, skipped or running.

## 🔒 What it never shows [#-what-it-never-shows]

A trace holds names and timings only. It has no message text, no tool details and no names of people. A turn from a temporary or Incognito chat has no trace.

**Turn trace** shows only for owners and admins, and not in an Incognito chat. You can also open `/trace/` followed by a turn's id on your Home address.

If it cannot load, it says "Could not load this trace." Tap **Try again**. A not-found answer means the turn is unknown or was private.

## 🙋 Still need help? [#-still-need-help]

For overall timing, use [Performance](/docs/admin/look-after-it/performance).


# Updates and rollback (/docs/admin/look-after-it/updates-and-rollback)

<Shot id="updates" />

## 🔍 What Home checks [#-what-home-checks]

Home asks GitHub once a day for the latest MaiPai Home release. If a robot is paired, it also checks the bot release. It sends no name or device ID.

Open **Settings**, **Home settings**, **Maintenance**, then **Updates**. The table has **Name**, **Installed**, **Available**, **Last checked** and **Status**. A row says **Up to date** or shows the newer version.

Only an owner or admin can manage updates.

## 🛠️ Update Home [#️-update-home]

Planned, not in the app yet: installing a Home update from this page. Home shows that one is available. You update it by hand.

1. Take a backup first. See [Backups and restore](/docs/admin/look-after-it/backups-and-restore).
2. Stop Home. If you run it from source, run `bun stop` in the Home folder. If you used the installer, stop the `maipai-home` service.
3. Install the new release from the GitHub release page, or pull the new tag if you run from source.
4. Run `bun install --force` if you run from source.
5. Start Home again.
6. Open **Updates** and check **Installed** shows the new version.

Planned, not in the app yet: a fixed update window and a kept previous release for one-click rollback of Home itself. To go back today, reinstall the earlier release and, if the data changed, restore the backup from step 1.

## ⚙️ Engines [#️-engines]

Rows for the AI engines (the Stack) have two buttons:

- **Apply** installs the update.
- **Go back** returns to the previous version after you confirm.

Choosing how reference library updates run, and capping their download speed, is planned, not available yet. The two settings exist but have no effect today.

## 📣 Get told [#-get-told]

Tick **Telegram me when a MaiPai Home update is available** and the engine update switches in your Notifications settings. See [Notifications and Telegram](/docs/admin/connect-and-extend/notifications-and-telegram).

## 🔧 If the check shows nothing [#-if-the-check-shows-nothing]

Home may have no internet, or GitHub may have limited the request. Wait a day and look again. Open **Repairs** for anything Home flags.


# Add people and parental controls (/docs/admin/people-and-safety/add-people-and-parental-controls)

This page is for owners and admins.

## 👤 Add a person [#-add-a-person]

<Shot id="roles-users" />

1. Open **Settings**, then **Home settings**, then **Users**.
2. Under **Add someone**, type the person's name.
3. Pick a **Role**. The list shows only the roles you may create. An admin sees adult, teen, child and guest. An owner also sees admin and owner.
4. For an owner, admin or adult, type a **PIN or password**. They use it to sign in. Teens, children and guests need none.
5. Press **Add to household**.

If you skip the PIN for a role that needs one, Home says "This role requires a PIN or password. Enter one above, then try again." If something else fails, Home says "Could not add that person." Check the name is filled in, then try again.

The person's age group follows the role. A child gets child controls, a teen gets teen controls. See [People, roles and permissions](/docs/admin/how-it-works/people-roles-and-permissions).

## ✏️ Change a role or remove someone [#️-change-a-role-or-remove-someone]

- Only the owner can change a role. Open **Users** and pick the new role next to the name.
- To lock a person's session after idle time, tick **Require PIN lock** next to the name and set the timeout in minutes. The default is 5.
- To remove someone, press **Remove**, then **Yes, remove**. Home shows how many files only that person could see. Those files are deleted with them. Files other people can see stay with the household. For a child, you can download their files first. A person's own files are private, so ask an adult to save theirs.
- Home will not remove or demote the only owner.

## 🧒 A child's controls [#-a-childs-controls]

Open **Family**, then the child's card. Two tabs are only for owners and admins:

| Tab | What you set |
|---|---|
| **Limits** | Daily minutes for each kind of app (Family, Fun, Health, Home, Info, Learning, Media, Robot body, Utilities). 0 means no limit. The minutes are saved but not applied yet. Also the child's storage. |
| **Topics** | **Sensitive subjects**. See [Safety settings](/docs/admin/people-and-safety/safety-settings). |

Changes save as you make them. The child cannot open either tab.

## 🧑 A teen's controls [#-a-teens-controls]

There is no per-teen screen. Teen settings are household-wide and sit under Settings, Privacy and Search. A teen's own profile, chats and settings are private from admins.

## 🤝 When a child has a hard moment [#-when-a-child-has-a-hard-moment]

Every adult gets a notice that "A check-in may help." It names the child and not what was said. This cannot be turned off.

## 🙋 Support [#-support]

- Someone cannot sign in: see [Cannot sign in](/docs/user/fix-a-problem/cannot-sign-in).
- To see what each role sees, see [What each role can do](/docs/user/your-family/what-each-role-can-do).


# Blocked-site lists and news feeds (/docs/admin/people-and-safety/blocked-sites-and-news-feeds)

This page is for owners and admins.

<Shot id="settings-search" />

## 🚫 Blocked-site lists [#-blocked-site-lists]

Web search checks every result against lists of sites that are blocked for the age group. Home downloads the lists from The Block List Project and refreshes them about monthly. It asks for the list index about daily. Neither request carries a name or device ID.

| List | Child | Teen | Adult |
|---|---|---|---|
| **Adult sites** | On, locked | On, locked | Off |
| **Gambling sites** | On | On | Off |
| **Scam sites** | On | On | Off |
| **Phishing sites** | On | On | Off |
| **Malware sites** | On | On | Off |
| **Drug sites** | On | Off | Off |

"Locked" means nobody can turn it off.

## ✍️ Change a list for one person [#️-change-a-list-for-one-person]

1. Open **Settings**, then **Home settings**, then **Search**.
2. Find **Blocked sites by person** and pick the **Person**.
3. The left column shows the global defaults. Tick or untick a box in the person's column.
4. To undo a change, use the reset link beside the row.

Rows you cannot change are the age group's setting, or a block that always stays on.

## 🌐 Your own site rules [#-your-own-site-rules]

Under the advanced Search settings you can add sites by hand, separated by commas, such as `example.com`:

- **Always block these sites** and **Allow these sites** apply to everyone.
- The same pair exists for child, teen and adult.

An allow entry shows a site even when a list has it. Use it sparingly for children.

## 📰 News feeds [#-news-feeds]

The News shelf on Home is on by default. Pick which feed lists each age group sees:

| Setting | Default |
|---|---|
| **News lists with child controls** | Kids' news |
| **News lists with teen controls** | Household news |
| **News lists with adult controls** | Household news |

To add your own, put the feed addresses in **Extra news feeds for** child, teen or adult. Each must start with `https://`.

Home polls feeds every 1800 seconds by default (900 is the minimum) and keeps 90 days of items. It reads only the feed file, never the articles. Each feed adds a row on the [privacy page](/docs/admin/look-after-it/privacy-audit).

## 🔧 When a list does not download [#-when-a-list-does-not-download]

Home shows a notice under Settings, Repairs. Check the computer has internet, then reopen Repairs. Search keeps working, using the lists it already has.

Planned, not in the app yet: importing your own blocklist files.


# Safety settings for children and teens (/docs/admin/people-and-safety/safety-settings)

This page is for owners and admins. Home gives children and teens stricter answers than adults. You can tune some of that. You cannot remove it.

## 🔒 What cannot be turned off [#-what-cannot-be-turned-off]

These stay the same for every child and teen, whatever you set:

- Age and surface checks come before everything else in a reply.
- Feelings and safety get care first, with a pointer to a trusted grown-up.
- Bullying, secrets and sharing where a child lives are never helped.
- On religion and politics, Home takes no side.
- If a child is in danger, Home points to a grown-up and the emergency number.
- The **Adult sites** blocklist is always on for children and teens.
- A child's hard-moment notice to adults. See [Add people](/docs/admin/people-and-safety/add-people-and-parental-controls).
- Reasoning text is never sent to a child or teen.
- Children's safe search is always strict. A teen's is never lower than moderate.

## 🎚️ What you can change for a child [#️-what-you-can-change-for-a-child]

Open **Family**, the child's card, then **Topics**. Each subject has a level:

| Subject | Choices |
|---|---|
| Bodies and relationships | **Follow child controls (recommended)**, **Gently point to you**, **Answer simply with correct body words** |
| Illness, death and health | **Follow child controls (recommended)**, **Answer gently and honestly**, **Gently point to you** |
| Drugs, alcohol, betting and dares | **Follow child controls (recommended)**, **Explain simply and kindly**, **Gently point to you** |
| Violence, weapons and scary news | **Follow child controls (recommended)**, **Answer gently, no gore**, **Gently point to you** |
| Santa Claus and other family stories | **Keep the stories (recommended)** or **Don't keep them**; edit **Names of family stories** |

Only an owner or admin can change these.

## 🧑 What you can change for every teen [#-what-you-can-change-for-every-teen]

These are household settings under **Settings**, then **Home settings**. The topic levels are under **Privacy**, the web search switch under **Search**, and the reply check under **Engines and AI**, **Chat**:

| Setting | Default | Effect |
|---|---|---|
| **Bodies and relationships with teen controls** | Answer factually | Factual and respectful, never sexual or romantic. Can be set to **Point to a trusted adult or doctor**. |
| **Drugs, alcohol and betting with teen controls** | Explain the real risks | Real risks and how to get help, never tips. Can be set to **Point to a trusted adult or doctor**. |
| **Web search with teen controls** | On | Off means offline library only. |
| **How a teen's replies are checked** | Sentence | Sentence checks every sentence before a teen sees it. Arrival shows text as it is written and checks it as it comes, so part of a sentence can show before its check ends. |

Children, and anything spoken, always check every sentence first. An admin cannot see what a teen asks.

## 🔎 Web search for minors [#-web-search-for-minors]

| Setting | Default |
|---|---|
| **Web search with child controls** | On: strictest SafeSearch, adult sites blocked, links hidden |
| **Page text check** | On for children and teens. They cannot turn it off. |

See [Web search](/docs/admin/connect-and-extend/web-search) and [Blocked-site lists](/docs/admin/people-and-safety/blocked-sites-and-news-feeds).

## ⚠️ If a setting looks greyed out [#️-if-a-setting-looks-greyed-out]

A lock means the setting belongs to the age group or the person. Ask the owner, or read the help text under the setting. A teen's own settings are not yours to change.
